questions.question: Q1. What is the primary engineering reason for keeping the drone's Center of Gravity (CG) aligned with its geometric center?

answers.a: To maximize the battery's cell voltage
answers.b: To ensure uniform motor loading and stable vertical thrust vectoring
answers.c: To reduce the airframe drag coefficient
answers.d: To increase the propeller's aerodynamic torque

explanations.a: Incorrect — Battery cell voltage is an electrochemical property and is independent of CG.
explanations.b: Correct — When CG is centered, all motors distribute the load equally, preventing asymmetric motor heating and ensuring symmetric flight control.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Drag coefficient depends on the shape of the frame and frontal area, not CG.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Aerodynamic torque is determined by propeller geometry and speed.

questions.question: Q2. In a quadcopter X-configuration, where is the reference datum origin (0,0) typically located for balancing calculations?

answers.b: At the bottom of the battery pack casing
answers.c: At the geometric center of the main deck frame hub
answers.d: At the tip of the longest propeller blade

explanations.a: Incorrect — Using a motor tip as origin is inconvenient and creates asymmetric coordinates.
explanations.b: Incorrect — The battery is a movable component and cannot act as a static reference datum.
explanations.c: Correct — The geometric center of the central plate structure is the standard origin (0,0) from which all coordinates (motors, battery, payload) are measured.
explanations.d: Incorrect — The rotating propeller tip is a dynamic, moving boundary.

questions.question: Q3. What is the mathematical definition of the Center of Gravity ($x_{\mathrm{CG}}$) along a single coordinate axis?

answers.a: The sum of all component positions divided by the number of components
answers.b: The product of the total weight and the maximum arm length
answers.c: The weighted average of component positions, solved as $x_{\mathrm{CG}} = \sum(m_i x_i) / \sum m_i$
answers.d: The square root of the sum of squared distances

explanations.a: Incorrect — This is a simple spatial average, which ignores the differences in component masses.
explanations.b: Incorrect — This is closer to a moment calculation, not a centroid.
explanations.c: Correct — The CG is the mass-weighted average position of all parts: $x_{\mathrm{CG}} = \sum(m_i \cdot x_i) / \sum m_i$.
explanations.d: Incorrect — This is the Euclidean distance formula.

questions.question: Q4. If a drone has a total mass of $1000\text{ g}$ and a battery of $400\text{ g}$ is shifted by $+20\text{ mm}$ along the Y-axis, how much does the drone's CG shift?

explanations.a: Correct — The shift in CG is given by $\Delta y = (m_{\mathrm{batt}} \cdot \Delta y_{\mathrm{batt}}) / M_{\mathrm{total}} = (400 \cdot 20) / 1000 = 8.0\text{ mm}$.
explanations.b: Incorrect — The drone's CG shift is scaled down by the mass fraction of the battery.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Calculated mass fraction division yields 8.0 mm, not 5.0 mm.
explanations.d: Incorrect — 10.0 mm is half the shift, not the mass-weighted shift.

questions.question: Q5. A quadcopter arm is clamped at the main body and loaded by thrust at the motor tip. What type of beam model best represents this structural setup?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Simply supported beams are pinned at both ends, whereas a drone arm is clamped at only one end.
explanations.b: Correct — A cantilever beam is fixed/clamped at one end (root at the body frame) and free to flex at the other end (loaded at the motor tip).
explanations.c: Incorrect — There are no intermediate supports along the span of a quadcopter arm.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Overhanging beams extend beyond two supports.

questions.question: Q6. In a cantilever beam of length $L$ subjected to a point force $F$ at the free tip, where does the maximum bending moment ($M_{\mathrm{max}}$) occur?

answers.b: Precisely midway along the span ($x = L/2$)
answers.d: It is constant along the entire span of the beam

explanations.a: Incorrect — Bending moment is zero at the free tip since the lever arm distance is zero.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Bending moment at mid-span is half of the maximum moment.
explanations.c: Correct — The bending moment is maximum at the clamped root because the tip load has the maximum possible lever arm distance ($M_{\mathrm{max}} = F \cdot L$).
explanations.d: Incorrect — Shear force is constant, but bending moment varies linearly.

questions.question: Q7. What is the dimension of the Bending Moment ($M$) in SI units?

explanations.a: Incorrect — N/m represents surface tension or stiffness constant, not torque/moment.
explanations.b: Correct — Bending moment is force multiplied by distance, which is measured in Newton-meters (N·m).
explanations.c: Incorrect — Megapascals is the unit for stress and pressure (N/mm^2).
explanations.d: Incorrect — This is the dimension of force in base units (Newtons).

questions.question: Q8. How does bending stress ($\sigma$) vary across the height/thickness of a beam under a bending load?

answers.a: It is constant across the entire cross-section
answers.b: It is zero at the Neutral Axis and increases linearly to maximum values at the outer fibers
answers.c: It is highest at the Neutral Axis and drops to zero at the surface
answers.d: It varies quadratically, peaking at the top fiber only

explanations.a: Incorrect — Bending stress is not uniform; fibers experience different degrees of tension/compression.
explanations.b: Correct — According to flexure theory (sigma = M*y/I), stress is zero at the neutral plane and scales linearly with distance y, peaking at the outermost boundaries.
explanations.c: Incorrect — This description represents shear stress distribution, not bending stress.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Bending stress is linear and symmetric across the neutral axis.

questions.question: Q9. What is the area moment of inertia ($I$) of a solid rectangular beam of width $b$ and height $h$?

explanations.a: Incorrect — This is the section modulus (S = I/c = b*h^2/6), not moment of inertia.
explanations.b: Correct — The area moment of inertia of a solid rectangle relative to its horizontal centroidal axis is $I = \frac{b \cdot h^3}{12}$.
explanations.c: Incorrect — The height h must be cubed since it is perpendicular to the bending axis.
explanations.d: Incorrect — This is for a triangular cross-section.

questions.question: Q10. How is the Safety Factor ($SF$) of a structural component calculated relative to yield strength?

explanations.a: Incorrect — This would result in values less than 1.0 for safe components.
explanations.b: Correct — The safety factor is the ratio of the material's yield strength to the maximum applied normal stress: $SF = \sigma_{\mathrm{yield}} / \sigma_{\mathrm{applied}}$.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Young's modulus affects stiffness and deflection, not yield safety factor directly.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Deflection ratio does not define structural yield safety factor.
